segments.text: Law is the broadest legal paper in Group VI. The official outline is short, but it expects familiarity with major civil, criminal, evidence and arbitration laws. The best approach is to understand the purpose and structure of each statute before learning important provisions.

items.text: Make a one-page map of each statute:
purpose, structure, key concepts and important stages.
Learn legal terms in plain English first; add section numbers only after the concept is clear.
identify the law, rule, application and conclusion.
Revise civil and criminal procedure as step-by-step flows rather than isolated provisions.

segments.text: Begin with the difference between substantive law and procedure. Then study civil procedure as a civil-case flow, criminal procedure as a criminal-case flow, evidence as the rules of proof, and the PPC as the rules defining offences. Arbitration and civil-court jurisdiction should be learned as separate process maps.
